sequencing.question: Which next-work sequence best preserves Can's explicit guarantees while making a coherent zero-compatibility redesign reviewable? Choose a process direction, not a language specification.
sequencing.before: Current normal gates pass, while F01/F02 leave acceptance/identity checks incomplete or ambiguous and F04/F05 fail integration. Type strings, source rules and TS layouts are coupled.

repair_then_core.design: Repair confirmed defects, establish shared type/core and boundary contracts, then migrate semantics in bounded green slices.
repair_then_core.benefit: Creates reliable evidence and shared rules before broad semantic changes.
repair_then_core.cost: Some existing parser/emitter work may later be replaced; visible simplification comes later.
repair_then_core.obligation: Keep independently reproduced failures visible, preserve source evidence identities, avoid treating a proposed core as an approved specification.
repair_then_core.after: F01 regression green -> typed representation and boundary decision -> uniform-success slice with full migrated corpus.

vertical_slice.design: First design and implement one end-to-end uniform-success/call slice, repairing defects it touches and extracting a core from that experience.
vertical_slice.benefit: Tests real customer pressure and avoids a speculative general core.
vertical_slice.cost: Cross-cutting evidence/identity defects remain until separately repaired; large slice may expose repeated work.
vertical_slice.obligation: No false green gate; explicitly track untouched F findings and preserve authority through temporary compiler staging.
vertical_slice.after: Choose one optional-map customer -> specify success semantics -> migrate parser/checker/evaluator/emitter/evidence together.

parallel_tracks.design: Run defect repairs and a bounded async/host prototype alongside semantic/core design; merge only through shared contracts.
parallel_tracks.benefit: Real host requirements can constrain the public ABI early, with parallel progress.
parallel_tracks.cost: Coordination and prototype discard cost; unsettled types/outcomes can invalidate experiments.
parallel_tracks.obligation: Prototype is not shipped language authority; settle shared ABI and all green gates before integration.
parallel_tracks.after: Repair F01/F02 alongside disposable B05 backend spikes against the same conformance matrix; use results in a later ABI decision.

repair_and_specify.design: Repair F01/F02/F04/F05 and publish an accurate current semantic inventory and gates before choosing a typed core or a vertical semantic migration.
repair_and_specify.benefit: Improves correctness and specification confidence without prematurely committing to a compiler architecture.
repair_and_specify.cost: Defers simplification and may perform repairs that a later redesign replaces.
repair_and_specify.obligation: Do not let inventory work excuse known defects; make any remaining semantic contradictions explicit and preserve distinct authority/evidence identities.
repair_and_specify.after: Make the current compiler and complete target bundles reliable, then decide core extraction versus success/call migration using concrete pressure cases.

successes.question: Which canonical success convention should be developed for Can, across calls, tests, scripts, contracts, generics and the public host boundary? The actual envelope/Unit specification still needs review.
successes.before: For Pair(int,bool), Ok(7,true) and Ok<Pair>(Pair(7,true)) both emit flattened fields; for int, Ok(7) emits value. Typed binders bind T; untyped scalar binders wrap it.

whole_value.design: Every function success contains one T; Ok(x) and its binder mean the whole value for records and scalars alike.
whole_value.benefit: One generic producer/consumer rule; preserves nominal record identity without B11-specific binder syntax.
whole_value.cost: All constructor/binder/contracts/catalogue/host layouts migrate; Unit and public envelope must be decided.
whole_value.obligation: No coercion or erased record identity; preserve error payloads, empty records and source evidence; separate public and private layout decisions.
whole_value.after: Proposed source: Ok(Pair(7,true)); on Ok(pair) binds Pair. The public tag/envelope and the private representation are separate unchosen contracts.

declared_shape.design: Keep declared-type-dependent record flattening and scalar value slots as the canonical rule; retain explicit whole-value typed forms for polymorphic code.
declared_shape.benefit: Direct access to result fields and shallow TS objects; current B11 already supports whole generic values.
declared_shape.cost: Two binder/construction conventions and shape-specific backend rules remain; benefit must justify complexity independently of compatibility.
declared_shape.obligation: Precisely align contracts, tests, empty/one-field records and generic instantiation; never silently splat a scalar or erase nominality.
declared_shape.after: Ok(7,true) for Pair; Ok<T>(value) in a generic producer; on Ok<T> x for whole-T consumers.

total_raw.design: Functions with no declared errors return raw T; fallible functions return an explicit outcome.
total_raw.benefit: Simpler total-function composition and potentially less wrapper work.
total_raw.cost: The error-set boundary changes application/result typing; becoming fallible is a larger interface migration.
total_raw.obligation: No inference of purity from empty errors; no hidden propagation; explicit adaptation for higher-order total/fallible signatures and tests. Empty declared errors do not imply absence of runtime faults.
total_raw.after: Proposed total identity: id(x) = x; fallible parse retains explicit Ok(parsed) or a qualified declared error such as json.invalid(payload).

calls.question: Which source application direction should Can develop while preserving explicit outcomes and target-sensitive authority/termination checks? Local binding and additional callable positions require their own rules.
calls.before: Named: match call f(x); indirect: match invoke cb with x. Factory-bound Fn values cannot simply be invoked in all local positions.

explicit_unified.design: One explicit call operation for named and typed callable targets, with the target's signature determining arguments and outcomes.
explicit_unified.benefit: Common application rule while keeping outcome-producing evaluation visibly marked.
explicit_unified.cost: Parser/core/call graph/scripts change; multi-parameter callbacks and new positions require additional analysis.
explicit_unified.obligation: Single evaluation, specified target/argument order, no implicit early exit; keep static versus indirect authority and cycle edges.
explicit_unified.after: Proposed: match call f(x) ...; match call cb(x) ...; typed target resolution distinguishes them.

bare_unified.design: Use f(x) uniformly for named and indirect application, with typing requiring exhaustive outcome use.
bare_unified.benefit: Conventional composition with less syntax; the type system supplies the operation distinction.
bare_unified.cost: Constructor/application parsing and diagnostics must stay clear; new expression positions can conceal evaluation effects from casual reading.
bare_unified.obligation: Same authority, cycles and outcome accounting as explicit calls; forbid implicit exception/return propagation.
bare_unified.after: Proposed: match f(x) ...; match cb(x) ...; a fallible application cannot be silently discarded.

retain_distinct.design: Keep separate named call and unary invoke syntax, while independently considering safe additional callable locations.
retain_distinct.benefit: Makes direct dependencies and indirect execution visibly different; aligns with the present bounded Fn design.
retain_distinct.cost: Generic consumers have two application rules and restricted composition remains unless expanded separately.
retain_distinct.obligation: Distinction must reflect useful authority/evidence facts rather than parameter-location accidents; preserve identical signature semantics.
retain_distinct.after: match call f(x) ... and match invoke cb with x ... remain canonical, with any new binder target explicitly analyzed.

modules.question: Which symbol ownership and module visibility direction best serves Can after fixing ambiguous declarations? All candidates must reject F02/F04 conflicts rather than coalescing them.
modules.before: Files list provides/uses with global __ names; every source function is exported in TS; duplicate records can first-win and incompatible error schemas coalesce until later payload checking fails.

scoped_symbols.design: Module-owned declarations with local names, explicit imports and public/private visibility; exact artifacts selected separately.
scoped_symbols.benefit: Clear ownership, independent short names and smaller public surfaces; cases include their parent identity.
scoped_symbols.cost: Resolver, brand owners, revisions, hosts, LSP and all sources migrate; moving a declaration needs identity policy.
scoped_symbols.obligation: Reject ambiguity, preserve mint/disclosure authority and declaring-owner host binding, detect stale/mixed artifacts.
scoped_symbols.after: Proposed: module ratio exports Ratio; import scalar as s; distinct ratio.nonterminating and s.nonterminating schemas.

owned_globals.design: Keep globally qualified identifiers, but add unique declaration owners, explicit visibility and deterministic import checks.
owned_globals.benefit: Retains self-describing names and simpler lookup while fixing actual collision and visibility defects.
owned_globals.cost: Long global names and source export metadata remain; ownership still needs a structured symbol identity.
owned_globals.obligation: No first-wins duplicates; one schema per error identity; prefixes are display names rather than authority proof.
owned_globals.after: ratio__divide and scalars__divide retain spellings; explicitly import one shared schema or use distinct qualified errors.

package_scope.design: Use package-level public identity and private file modules, with explicit package manifests selecting artifacts.
package_scope.benefit: File moves can be private refactors; public authority is owned at a stable package boundary.
package_scope.cost: Introduces a package concept and choices about intra-package trust, brand grants and revisions.
package_scope.obligation: Define which scope mints brands and owns hosts; never equate package reachability with permission.
package_scope.after: Proposed package std.math exports divide; implementation file ratio may move without changing the package declaration identity.

strict_global.design: Keep one global namespace and current provides/uses, but reject every duplicate definition at its declaration; defer visibility redesign.
strict_global.benefit: The smallest deterministic repair, retaining a simple explicit dependency model.
strict_global.cost: Long globally unique names, helper exports and limited independent package vocabulary remain.
strict_global.obligation: One owner/schema per global identity, explicit reuse through imports, source-order-independent CLI/LSP/checker/emitter/revision behavior; do not treat spelling as brand authorization.
strict_global.after: Shared__Record is declared once and imported; two distinct types need distinct global names; helper exports remain a consciously accepted limit.

pure_source_tests.question: Which default testing contract should Can develop for cross-file checked pure source, keeping unit/mock, integration and proof evidence distinct?
pure_source_tests.before: Same-file source executes in ordinary rows; cross-file source uses exchange scripts. Linked-pure execution exists as a separate path with its own evidence limits.

execute_pure.design: Execute checked pure Can source independent of file location; require explicit contract mocks and script real observations.
execute_pure.benefit: Helper extraction does not change default behavior; tests exercise real pure composition.
execute_pure.cost: Larger evaluated dependency closure, potentially slower rows and more change coupling; old mock tests need explicit intent.
execute_pure.obligation: Do not execute hosts at compile time; stabilize effect-site scripts, fresh state and provider preparation; never credit integration runs as local witnesses by accident. Admission examines the full reachable graph: no extern/state/effects, only admitted deterministic kernels; empty emits alone is insufficient.
execute_pure.after: Moving pure validate from quota.can to scalars.can preserves row execution; a deliberate mock is marked explicitly.

contract_boundary.design: Keep imported-source calls scripted by default, and require separate linked integration gates.
contract_boundary.benefit: Tests isolate producer contracts and remain stable/fast when imported bodies change.
contract_boundary.cost: File movement changes test obligations and mocks may hide real composition defects.
contract_boundary.obligation: Make unit versus linked results explicit; require representative actual dependency execution and complete request/response scripts.
contract_boundary.after: Quota rows script scalar__validate; an independent committed linked integration vector runs the real validator and checks composition.

explicit_test_modes.design: Require rows/suites to declare unit-contract or linked-source mode rather than derive behavior from file location.
explicit_test_modes.benefit: Test intent is visible and both isolation and integration remain available.
explicit_test_modes.cost: Another declaration and coverage policy; authors may choose the easier mode without meaningful integration gates.
explicit_test_modes.obligation: Define admission/credit for each mode, prevent real-host execution, and keep moved helpers semantically stable within a mode.
explicit_test_modes.after: Proposed unit row mocks a selected pure boundary; linked row executes all admitted pure providers across files.

host_boundary.question: Which public JavaScript embedding policy should Can specify, independently of private layout and wire codecs? Current hosts are trusted; a stronger public boundary is a proposed product choice.
host_boundary.before: Direct exported TS functions receive arrays/objects/callbacks; alias mutation, getters and a raw effectful JS callback occur in F03. TS types erase brands/decimal validity.

validated_owned.design: Default public entries validate admitted values and acquire defined ownership/snapshots; expose readonly/opaque TS facades and checked callable provenance.
validated_owned.benefit: Public source guarantees have an enforceable ingress boundary rather than depending on arbitrary host objects.
validated_owned.cost: Validation/copy overhead and adapter complexity; proxies/getters/cycles, resource limits and authority need explicit policy.
validated_owned.obligation: Shape is not minting authority; no typeof-function purity certificate; define reentry, host faults, post-completion mutation and trusted opt-in paths.
validated_owned.after: Public facade accepts validated copied [1n]; later host mutation does not change Can's completed value; branded entry requires authorized construction.

trusted_documented.design: Specify a deliberately trusted embedding contract with direct generated entry calls and explicit host ownership/provenance responsibilities.
trusted_documented.benefit: Minimal wrapper cost and a simple deployment model for controlled hosts.
trusted_documented.cost: Cannot enforce immutability/purity against a violating embedding; all application integrators must uphold the contract.
trusted_documented.obligation: Document alias/callback/fault responsibilities honestly, version artifacts, and avoid claiming source guarantees for arbitrary JS inputs.
trusted_documented.after: Host promises exclusive immutable use of an array after transfer and only compiler-produced callbacks; violations are embedding faults.

data_only_facade.design: Start with a validated data-only public facade; keep Fn, state handles and authority-bearing values private or reachable through explicit capabilities.
data_only_facade.benefit: Smaller enforceable boundary and simpler conformance testing than arbitrary public callable provenance.
data_only_facade.cost: Restricts public higher-order APIs and requires wrappers/handles for some integrations; validation/copy still costs.
data_only_facade.obligation: Separate codec data from authorized nominal values; maintain exact numbers and explicit errors; define per-world state/reentry.
data_only_facade.after: Expose parse(data) through a schema adapter; public map accepts a declared operation handle only if a later capability design admits it.

error_abstraction.question: What next error-composition direction should Can pursue for reusable generic combinators, while retaining complete declared failures and distinguishing returned domain errors from runtime faults?
error_abstraction.before: Concrete emits lists and Fn error lists are finite; no generic error rows or completed Outcome data. Per-error wrappers duplicate map/recover logic.

rows_and_outcomes.design: Design finite error-row algebra plus first-class completed Outcome<T,E>, with explicit handling/preservation/transfer/discard semantics.
rows_and_outcomes.benefit: Supports generic map, and_then, map_error, zip and collect while retaining payload types.
rows_and_outcomes.cost: New kinds, variance, consumption/catalogue rules and nested outcome semantics; much larger proof and boundary surface.
rows_and_outcomes.obligation: One declaration for the function's own failure boundary; Outcome as successful data remains nested; no generic catch-all silently loses a new error.
rows_and_outcomes.after: Proposed map<T,U,E>(Outcome<T,E>, mapper) returns Outcome<U,E>. Any zip collecting simultaneous failures needs an explicit error product/collection; a simple row union alone cannot represent both.

rows_first.design: Add generic finite error rows and explicit generic relay at control-flow boundaries before making outcomes storable data.
rows_first.benefit: Enables reusable fallible callable composition while limiting new failure-as-data accounting.
rows_first.cost: Some zip/collect/inspection APIs remain awkward; eventual completed outcomes may require another migration.
rows_first.obligation: Specify row union/subsumption and relay as preservation, not catch-all recovery; preserve all payloads and witnesses.
rows_first.after: Proposed compose(f: Fn<A,B,E>, g: Fn<B,C,F>) emits union(E,F), relaying each failure without exposing raw outcome storage.

concrete_combinators.design: Keep concrete declared errors for now and add explicitly specialized domain combinators while gathering pressure cases.
concrete_combinators.benefit: Small proven core, clear exhaustiveness and lower initial implementation burden.
concrete_combinators.cost: Duplication and limited library abstraction; every new domain/error set needs more source.
concrete_combinators.obligation: Do not erase errors into str/any or confuse test instances with generic proofs; record pressure cases as deferred capability.
concrete_combinators.after: A JSON-specific recover function handles only json.invalid with its payload; another error set needs a separate checked function.

b05_process.question: Which B05 ABI decision process should happen next, given the supplied competing Promise and private-machine proposals? This question does not choose final syntax or declare either proposal implemented.
b05_process.before: Current output is synchronous. Proposal A uses a uniform completion-capable callable ABI (Promise is one possible lowering), labeled join slots, singleton joins, dynamic completes deadline, declared rejects error, and concurrency isolated; it has no separate settlement bound. Proposal B uses a private frame machine for join-capable worlds, positional slots/local site IDs, only completion-contracted extern singleton, Host__World.use, one active root, literal timeout T and settle S, and runtime receipt/reentry/world-fault rules. A fully join-free B artifact may keep direct output. These are competing unimplemented source and host contracts, not merely interchangeable backends. Resources still need acquisition/use/release/cleanup rules.

contract_then_compare.design: First settle common source/ownership/settlement and public root contracts, then compare bounded Promise and machine prototypes against identical conformance and cost cases.
contract_then_compare.benefit: Separates semantic requirements from backend choice; collects implementation evidence before committing.
contract_then_compare.cost: Two prototypes and delayed final ABI choice; risks overdesign without a real customer slice.
contract_then_compare.obligation: First resolve the source and host disagreements: labels/positions/singletons; rejection as domain error versus embedding fault; timer expiry versus settlement; all children registered, complete outcomes, authority retained through cleanup. Then test duplicate/late receipts, slot overwrite, reentry/concurrent roots, alias mutation/late effects, simultaneous failures, final store, resource exhaustion and scheduler progress.
contract_then_compare.after: The same two-child failure/late-effect/reentry tests run through both prototypes before a private execution decision.

promise_reference.design: Use proposal A's uniform completion-capable internal callable ABI as a reference prototype, possibly with Promises; specify the public adapter separately and ratify neither syntax nor ABI yet.
promise_reference.benefit: Uses mature JS host integration and reaches a real async customer sooner.
promise_reference.cost: Completion allocation/scheduling and rejection semantics need measurement. Backend replacement still requires whole-world re-emission or an explicit bridge and conformance parity; prototype details may harden into accidental ABI.
promise_reference.obligation: Explicitly decide whether to strengthen A with settlement-before-completion and fault handling; it cannot be credited with B's T/S guarantee today. Evaluate full join outcomes, host rejection, duplicate completion, cleanup, reentry and nonpreemptible bigint work.
promise_reference.after: A disposable completion-returning internal implementation runs a real customer and failure vectors; the public root adapter is a separate decision.

machine_reference.design: Use proposal B's private frame/machine as the first reference prototype, with public root adapters hiding it; ratify neither source nor ABI yet.
machine_reference.benefit: Provides explicit receipt slots, reentry rules and world lifecycle state; any stack/allocation benefit remains unmeasured.
machine_reference.cost: Custom runtime/interpreter complexity and larger trusted machinery before practical performance evidence.
machine_reference.obligation: Prove transition and continuation invariants, handle duplicate completions and malformed hosts, preserve full joins and honest settlement.
machine_reference.after: Root facade drives private frames; two pending children settle into a complete product before the root completion fires.

customer_contract_first.design: Choose one real async/resource customer and settle its source, authority, timeout/settlement and cleanup contracts; defer private runtime choice until acceptance vectors and measurements justify one or both spikes.
customer_contract_first.benefit: Grounds the design in real demand without assuming two backends or a runtime choice are needed now.
customer_contract_first.cost: Delays broad async availability and may optimize first for one customer.
customer_contract_first.obligation: Make all A/B source and host disagreements explicit, keep resources separate but accounted for, and do not promise liveness without a progressing platform.
customer_contract_first.after: Specify an HTTP request lifecycle with cancellation/cleanup and late-effect tests, then decide which bounded execution experiment could resolve an actual uncertainty.

contextual_typing.question: Where should Can allow contextual typing while preserving explicit API/authority contracts and nominal exact types? No candidate may infer a contract from tests.
contextual_typing.before: B11 writes Ok<T>(x) and on Ok<T> x; generic calls/tests and Seq constructors often repeat explicit type arguments.

local_context.design: Use deterministic bidirectional checking where expected type uniquely determines local constructor/pattern/application annotations; retain explicit API and ambiguous local annotations.
local_context.benefit: Less redundant syntax with a unique elaboration that tools can show.
local_context.cost: Context propagation and diagnostics become more complex; edits to enclosing types can affect locals.
local_context.obligation: No overload guessing, numeric coercion or nominal collapse; empty/polymorphic ambiguity demands annotation; explicit and inferred forms elaborate equivalently.
local_context.after: Proposed in -> Box<int>: Ok(Box(7)); without expected element type an empty Seq still needs Seq<int>[].

explicit_all.design: Keep explicit type applications and typed binders even when context appears unique.
explicit_all.benefit: Local syntax records the intended specialization and is easy to inspect without context.
explicit_all.cost: Repeated types add editing burden and more opportunities for inconsistent annotation; benefits need measurement.
explicit_all.obligation: Centralize type checking and give precise mismatch diagnostics; do not confuse verbosity with proof.
explicit_all.after: Ok<Box<int>>(Box<int>(7)); on Ok<Box<int>> result remains explicit.

constructor_context.design: Infer only constructors and patterns from a directly declared boundary; require explicit generic call/ref specializations.
constructor_context.benefit: A smaller inference surface removes obvious repetition while keeping specialization demands explicit.
constructor_context.cost: A deliberate rule boundary leaves some repeated types and another distinction for authors.
constructor_context.obligation: Document exactly which positions propagate expected types; preserve nominality and refuse ambiguity consistently.
constructor_context.after: Proposed -> Box<int> accepts Ok(Box(7)), but call id<int>(7) and fnref map<int>(...) stay explicit.

collection_spelling.question: Which collection type spelling should Can develop assuming the same compositional type and containment rules underneath? Do not infer nesting support from punctuation.
collection_spelling.before: Current Seq<T> has typed literals Seq<int>[1,2], while nested generic positions have separate implementation restrictions.

regular_application.design: Retain Seq<T> as the regular application grammar alongside Option<T> and Map<K,V>.
regular_application.benefit: One type application model and direct relation to generic libraries.
regular_application.cost: More punctuation for nested sequences; parser must distinguish type angles from comparisons.
regular_application.obligation: Compositional AST/substitution/containment and exact nominal identities; spelling alone solves no nesting defect.
regular_application.after: Proposed uniform nesting: Seq<Seq<int>> and Seq<Option<int>> under shared type rules.

bracket_sequence.design: Make [T] the one sequence type spelling, retaining Name<T> for other applications.
bracket_sequence.cost: A special type constructor grammar and migration of signatures/literals/tooling; [] already serves enumeration roles.
bracket_sequence.obligation: Specify context-disambiguation and canonical formatting; provide the same nesting/containment support as regular application.
bracket_sequence.after: Proposed [[int]] and [Option<int>] denote the same types as nested Seq applications.

postfix_sequence.design: Use T[] as the single sequence type spelling.
postfix_sequence.benefit: Familiar from TS target types and compact multi-dimensional spelling.
postfix_sequence.cost: Special precedence with Fn/generic types and expression indexing; target familiarity is not usability evidence.
postfix_sequence.obligation: Specify parenthesization and identical source immutability/type rules, independent of mutable TS array layout.
postfix_sequence.after: Proposed int[][] and Option<int>[] replace Seq<Seq<int>> and Seq<Option<int>>.

literals.question: Which literal-family direction should Can evaluate? Every candidate preserves exact int/dec, no coercions or rounding, and no Unicode normalization. A usability conclusion needs measured trials.
literals.before: Exact decimals use d"12.50"; ordinary strings are raw; e"line\n" decodes supported escapes.

conventional_exact.design: Ordinary dotted numeric tokens denote exact dec; ordinary strings decode a specified escape set and a prefixed form is raw.
conventional_exact.benefit: Familiar writing/editing conventions without introducing binary float.
conventional_exact.cost: Lexer, escaping, source tools and corpus migrate; leading/trailing dots, exponents and raw delimiter rules need decisions.
conventional_exact.obligation: Canonical decimal values and string scalar validation stay exact; formatter round trips and escaped/raw equivalence are tested.
conventional_exact.after: Proposed 12.50 denotes exact dec; "line\n" contains LF; r"line\n" contains backslash+n.

explicit_families.design: Keep prefixed exact decimal and interpreted-string forms with raw ordinary strings.
explicit_families.benefit: The numeric/text interpretation is visible and raw source minimizes escaping in many embedded fragments.
explicit_families.cost: Unfamiliar defaults can cause mistakes; decimal text resembles a string even though it is typed dec.
explicit_families.obligation: Measure actual agent mistakes, document escape families and retain strict Unicode/canonical numeric checks.
explicit_families.after: d"12.50", e"line\n" and raw "line\n" remain distinct canonical families.

numeric_only.design: Adopt ordinary exact decimal tokens but retain raw ordinary and e-prefixed interpreted strings.
numeric_only.benefit: Removes decimal quoting without simultaneously changing embedded-text defaults.
numeric_only.cost: Mixed conventionality and two independent syntax migrations over time if strings later change.
numeric_only.obligation: Do not couple string defaults to numeric semantics; test numeric lexer and unchanged string behavior independently.

boolean_evaluation.question: Which and/or evaluation policy should Can prefer pending agent trials, considering faulting pure expressions and source branch evidence? Ordinary function arguments remain strict in every option.
boolean_evaluation.before: and/or evaluate both operands. false and xs[0] == 1 can still fault on an empty sequence; explicit match is required to guard evaluation.

eager.design: Keep left-to-right eager and/or, using explicit match for guarded evaluation.
eager.benefit: Preserves uniform eager expressions and makes all control-flow branch obligations explicit in source matches.
eager.cost: Differs from many languages; guard-shaped boolean expressions can unexpectedly fault and require longer matches.
eager.obligation: Document eager fault behavior and test it in evaluator/TS; measure agent confusion rather than assuming explicitness succeeds.
eager.after:
Current guard shape:
match #xs == 0
  true => Ok(false)
  false => Ok(xs[0] == 1)

short_circuit.design: Make and/or left-to-right conditional evaluation with explicit typed-core guard nodes.
short_circuit.benefit: Natural safe boolean guards and familiar evaluation expectations.
short_circuit.cost: Introduces implicit source branches and changes fault/evaluation behavior; evidence obligations must be specified.
short_circuit.obligation: Preserve source origins and distinguish skipped from executed evidence; no lazy argument semantics or hidden error propagation.
short_circuit.after: Proposed #xs > 0 and xs[0] == 1 skips indexing for empty xs; coverage records the skipped/evaluated paths under the chosen rule.

explicit_conditional_operator.design: Replace eager and/or with a visibly conditional canonical spelling such as and_then/or_else for boolean expressions.
explicit_conditional_operator.benefit: Communicates conditional evaluation directly without keeping two synonymous families.
explicit_conditional_operator.cost: Unfamiliar names and corpus migration; still needs all short-circuit evidence rules and can be confused with outcome combinators.
explicit_conditional_operator.obligation: One operator family, stable evaluation and fault semantics; test readability before ratification.
explicit_conditional_operator.after: Proposed #xs > 0 and_then xs[0] == 1 uses an explicit conditional operator.

argument_labels.question: What should canonical Can tooling do with argument labels under one binding/evaluation rule? Labels are not permission to reorder effectful evaluation.
argument_labels.before: The structural lint rejects redundant in-position names; useful labels can be forced away even when authors intend readability.

preserve_optional.design: Allow named and positional arguments with one deterministic binding rule; preserve user labels in formatting.
preserve_optional.benefit: Names clarify similar-typed inputs while short obvious calls remain concise.
preserve_optional.cost: Multiple surface spellings conflict with the current canonical-form preference; positional/named mixing needs precise diagnostics.
preserve_optional.obligation: Duplicate/missing/unknown binding rejection, defined source evaluation order and formatting without semantic rewrites.
preserve_optional.after: Proposed transfer(from = source, to = destination) stays labeled even in declaration order; id(x) remains positional.

canonical_positional.design: Require positional arguments whenever each argument occupies its declared slot; retain names only where semantically required by the chosen binding rule.
canonical_positional.benefit: One compact normal form and less annotation churn.
canonical_positional.cost: Similar-typed arguments lose visible roles; structural lint forces readability edits unrelated to program correctness.
canonical_positional.obligation: Measure swapped-argument errors and diagnostic quality; canonicalization must not alter evaluation order or authority.
canonical_positional.after: transfer(from = source, to = destination) is diagnosed with canonical transfer(source, destination).

all_named.design: Require labels on all multi-argument calls/constructors, with an explicitly specified unary/empty convention.
all_named.benefit: Roles are visible and declaration reordering need not silently rebind arguments.
all_named.cost: More source and parameter-name API churn; repetitive mechanical labels in small helpers.
all_named.obligation: Parameter names become interface identity; define named source order, duplicate binding checks and canonical formatting.
all_named.after: Proposed transfer(from = source, to = destination) is required for a two-parameter declaration.
